# DaZ-Pilot – Docker Compose env vars.
# Copy to .env and fill in the secrets:  cp .env.example .env

# ── Environment ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
ENVIRONMENT=development
LOG_LEVEL=info
LOG_LEVEL_HTTP=info
SEND_SERVER_ERROR_MESSAGE=false

# ── Published host ports ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Only read by docker-compose.local.yml. The base stack publishes nothing.
# Postgres defaults to 5433 so it does not collide with a host installation.
POSTGRES_PORT=5433
ML_SERVICE_PORT=8000
BACKEND_PORT=4000
DASHBOARD_PORT=3000

# ── Server / CORS ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Public URL at which the core-backend serves the API (used for absolute URLs).
CORE_BACKEND_DOMAIN=http://localhost:4000
# Origin allowed by CORS (mobile app / dashboard).
FRONTEND_DOMAIN=http://localhost:3000
# Baked into the dashboard client bundle at build time (for Next.js Image remotePatterns).
NEXT_PUBLIC_CORE_BACKEND_DOMAIN=http://localhost:4000
# Optional. On-premises single-school installs: dashboard skips the school-slug
# screen and opens this school's login. Leave empty for multi-school hosting.
SCHOOL_SLUG=

# Number of reverse proxies in front of the API. 0 when reachable directly,
# 1 behind a single nginx/Caddy/Traefik. Too low and every client shares one
# rate-limit bucket; too high and clients can spoof X-Forwarded-For.
TRUST_PROXY=0

# Requests per client IP per 15 minutes across all /auth routes; one login costs
# four. Whenever TRUST_PROXY cannot tell clients apart (a school behind one NAT
# gateway), the whole site shares this budget — raise it for classroom use.
AUTH_RATE_LIMIT_MAX=60

# ── Database ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
DB_USER=daz
DB_PASS=daz-dev-password
DB_NAME=daz
DB_SSL=false
DB_POOL_SIZE=10
DB_DEBUG_SLOW_DB_ACCESS=0
DB_MAX_DEADLOCKS=100

# ── ML-Service ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# "auto" resolves to CPU in containers. Override to "cuda" for GPU hosts.
ML_DEVICE=auto
ML_SERVICE_TIMEOUT_MS=120000

# ── Media storage & ingest ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
MEDIA_PUBLIC_PATH=/media
# Signs the time-limited media URLs. Must be 32 bytes, base64 (the placeholder
# below happens to decode to exactly that). Generate:  openssl rand -base64 32
MEDIA_URL_SIGNING_KEY=replace-with-32-random-bytes-base64-encoded
FRAME_EXTRACTION_FPS=3
FRAME_EXTRACTION_CANDIDATES_PER_FRAME=3

# ── Secrets ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Both values below are throwaway defaults so that `cp .env.example .env` plus
# `docker compose up` works out of the box. Replace them in any deployment.

# Min. 64 characters. Generate:  openssl rand -hex 48
SUPER_ADMIN_API_KEY=dev-only-super-admin-api-key-replace-in-production-0000000000000000

# Encrypts the per-school OIDC client secrets at rest — anyone holding this key
# can decrypt them. Must be 32 bytes, base64. Generate:  openssl rand -base64 32
SECRETS_ENCRYPTION_KEY=ZGV2LW9ubHkta2V5LW5vdC1mb3ItcHJvZHVjdGlvbiE=

# ── SMTP ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Email OTP is the only login that works without an identity provider, so a
# reachable mail server is mandatory in every deployment. There are no working
# defaults here — fill in a real relay.
#
# Port 465 means implicit TLS, anything else negotiates STARTTLS.
#
# Locally you can skip the mail server: SMTP_ENABLED=false together with
# ENVIRONMENT=development writes the login code into the backend log instead of
# sending it. In any other environment the code is silently discarded.
SMTP_ENABLED=true
SMTP_HOST=smtp.example.org
SMTP_PORT=587
SMTP_USERNAME=
SMTP_PASSWORD=
SMTP_FROM_EMAIL=noreply@example.org
SMTP_FROM_NAME=DaZ-Pilot

# ── Mobile app links ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Served in /.well-known/assetlinks.json and /apple-app-site-association so the
# OIDC callback can hand off from the browser to the installed app. Leave empty
# until the store credentials exist; the callback then stays in the browser.
UPLOAD_KEY_FINGERPRINT=
PLAY_APP_SIGNING_FINGERPRINT=
APPLE_APP_TEAM_ID=

# ── Backups ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# The `backup` service starts with the stack and backs up Postgres, Qdrant and
# media_data online (no downtime). See infra/backup/BACKUP.md.
BACKUP_SCHEDULE=0 3 * * *
BACKUP_RETENTION_DAYS=30
# age public key from `age-keygen`. Without it the service exits on start —
# set BACKUP_ALLOW_PLAINTEXT=true only for local, throwaway data.
AGE_RECIPIENT=
BACKUP_ALLOW_PLAINTEXT=false
# Identity file is only needed for restore (mount it; do not commit it):
# AGE_IDENTITY_FILE=/run/age/identity
# Optional; default 600. Raise for large Qdrant snapshots.
# BACKUP_QDRANT_TIMEOUT_SEC=600
# TZ=UTC

# DaZ-Pilot stack. Env vars from .env (copy from .env.example).
#
# This file publishes nothing on the host: every service is only reachable from
# inside the compose network, so a deployment needs a reverse proxy that joins
# the network and routes to `backend:4000` and `dashboard:3000`. That makes it
# the file to hand to a server or to Coolify unchanged.
#
# Start deployment stack (npm run docker:up):
#   docker compose up -d --build
#
# Start with host ports for local work (npm run docker:local):
#   docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.local.yml up --build
#
# Start with host ports and hot-reload (npm run docker:dev):
#   docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.local.yml \
#     -f docker-compose.dev.yml up --build
#
# The `backup` service starts with the stack (see infra/backup/BACKUP.md) and
# requires AGE_RECIPIENT in .env. One-off run:
#   docker compose run --rm backup backup.sh
#
# Personal additions (Adminer, …) go in docker-compose.override.yml (gitignored)
# — auto-loaded when starting from the repo root without -f.

# Env shared by `backend` and `worker` (same image, different command).
x-backend-env: &backend-env
  NODE_ENV: production
  ENVIRONMENT: ${ENVIRONMENT:-production}
  LOG_LEVEL: ${LOG_LEVEL:-info}
  LOG_LEVEL_HTTP: ${LOG_LEVEL_HTTP:-info}
  NETWORK_INTERFACE: 0.0.0.0
  PORT: 4000
  WORKER_PORT: 4001
  # Number of reverse proxies in front of the API. Must match the deployment or
  # the auth rate limiters bucket every caller together (0) or trust a spoofable
  # X-Forwarded-For (too high).
  TRUST_PROXY: ${TRUST_PROXY:-0}
  # Requests per client IP per 15 minutes across *all* /auth routes. One login
  # costs four of them. Whenever TRUST_PROXY cannot separate clients, a whole
  # school shares one bucket — raise this before a class logs in at once.
  AUTH_RATE_LIMIT_MAX: ${AUTH_RATE_LIMIT_MAX:-60}
  CORE_BACKEND_DOMAIN: ${CORE_BACKEND_DOMAIN}
  FRONTEND_DOMAIN: ${FRONTEND_DOMAIN}
  SEND_SERVER_ERROR_MESSAGE: ${SEND_SERVER_ERROR_MESSAGE:-false}
  DB_HOST: postgres
  DB_PORT: 5432
  DB_USER: ${DB_USER}
  DB_PASS: ${DB_PASS}
  DB_NAME: ${DB_NAME}
  DB_SSL: ${DB_SSL:-false}
  DB_POOL_SIZE: ${DB_POOL_SIZE:-10}
  DB_DEBUG_SLOW_DB_ACCESS: ${DB_DEBUG_SLOW_DB_ACCESS:-0}
  DB_MAX_DEADLOCKS: ${DB_MAX_DEADLOCKS:-100}
  QDRANT_HOST: qdrant
  QDRANT_PORT: 6333
  ML_SERVICE_URL: http://ml-service:8000
  ML_SERVICE_TIMEOUT_MS: ${ML_SERVICE_TIMEOUT_MS:-120000}
  MEDIA_STORAGE_DIR: /app/media
  MEDIA_PUBLIC_PATH: ${MEDIA_PUBLIC_PATH:-/media}
  MEDIA_URL_SIGNING_KEY: ${MEDIA_URL_SIGNING_KEY}
  FRAME_EXTRACTION_FPS: ${FRAME_EXTRACTION_FPS:-5}
  FRAME_EXTRACTION_CANDIDATES_PER_FRAME: ${FRAME_EXTRACTION_CANDIDATES_PER_FRAME:-3}
  SUPER_ADMIN_API_KEY: ${SUPER_ADMIN_API_KEY}
  SECRETS_ENCRYPTION_KEY: ${SECRETS_ENCRYPTION_KEY}
  # Without SMTP the email OTP is generated, stored and then dropped — the only
  # login that works without an identity provider breaks silently. Default on so
  # a misconfigured mail server fails loudly instead.
  SMTP_ENABLED: ${SMTP_ENABLED:-true}
  SMTP_HOST: ${SMTP_HOST}
  SMTP_PORT: ${SMTP_PORT:-587}
  SMTP_USERNAME: ${SMTP_USERNAME}
  SMTP_PASSWORD: ${SMTP_PASSWORD}
  SMTP_FROM_EMAIL: ${SMTP_FROM_EMAIL}
  SMTP_FROM_NAME: ${SMTP_FROM_NAME:-DaZ-Pilot}
  # Served in /.well-known/assetlinks.json and /apple-app-site-association.
  # Required for the OIDC redirect to reach the mobile app via app links —
  # without them the callback dead-ends in the browser.
  UPLOAD_KEY_FINGERPRINT: ${UPLOAD_KEY_FINGERPRINT:-}
  PLAY_APP_SIGNING_FINGERPRINT: ${PLAY_APP_SIGNING_FINGERPRINT:-}
  APPLE_APP_TEAM_ID: ${APPLE_APP_TEAM_ID:-}

# `backend`, `worker` and `migrate` all use the same image.
# The `image:` tag lets Compose build it once and reuse it across the three services.
x-backend-build: &backend-build
  image: daz-pilot-backend:latest
  build:
    context: ./backend
    dockerfile: Dockerfile

services:
  postgres:
    image: postgres:17-alpine
    restart: unless-stopped
    volumes:
      - postgres_data:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: ${DB_USER}
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${DB_PASS}
      POSTGRES_DB: ${DB_NAME}
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U ${DB_USER} -d ${DB_NAME}"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 10

  qdrant:
    image: qdrant/qdrant:v1.14.0
    restart: unless-stopped
    volumes:
      - qdrant_storage:/qdrant/storage
      # Shared with `backup` so restore.sh can recover via file:///qdrant/snapshots/...
      - qdrant_snapshots:/qdrant/snapshots
    healthcheck:
      # Qdrant ships without curl/wget — probe via bash /dev/tcp.
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "bash -c '>/dev/tcp/127.0.0.1/6333' || exit 1"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 10

  ml-service:
    build:
      context: ./ml-service
      dockerfile: Dockerfile
    restart: unless-stopped
    expose:
      - "8000"
    environment:
      QDRANT_HOST: qdrant
      QDRANT_PORT: 6333
      # "auto" -> CPU in containers; override to "cuda" for GPU hosts.
      ML_DEVICE: ${ML_DEVICE:-auto}
      # Embed batch size = scan-latency knob. The embedder frees its slot at
      # every batch boundary, so a scan arriving mid-ingest waits at most one
      # batch. Default 8 (not the service default 32) keeps that wait ~10 s on
      # CPU-only hosts; raise it on GPU where throughput benefits from 32.
      EMBED_BATCH_SIZE: ${EMBED_BATCH_SIZE:-8}
      AUG_PRESET: ${AUG_PRESET:-off}
      AUG_COUNT: ${AUG_COUNT:-0}
      MIN_CONFIDENCE_RATIO: ${MIN_CONFIDENCE_RATIO:-1.5}
      # Persist the HuggingFace model cache so SigLIP (4.6 GB) isn't re-downloaded on restart.
      HF_HOME: /cache/huggingface
      TRANSFORMERS_CACHE: /cache/huggingface
    volumes:
      - ml_model_cache:/cache/huggingface
    depends_on:
      qdrant:
        condition: service_healthy
    healthcheck:
      # start_period is generous: first run downloads 4.6 GB of SigLIP weights.
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "curl -fsS http://localhost:8000/health || exit 1"]
      interval: 15s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5
      start_period: 300s

  # One-shot migration — runs before the backend, then exits.
  # Native dev workflow uses `npm run database:migrate` instead.
  migrate:
    <<: *backend-build
    restart: "no"
    command: ["npm", "run", "start:migrate"]
    environment:
      NODE_ENV: production
      ENVIRONMENT: ${ENVIRONMENT:-production}
      DB_HOST: postgres
      DB_PORT: 5432
      DB_USER: ${DB_USER}
      DB_PASS: ${DB_PASS}
      DB_NAME: ${DB_NAME}
      DB_SSL: ${DB_SSL:-false}
    depends_on:
      postgres:
        condition: service_healthy

  backend:
    <<: *backend-build
    restart: unless-stopped
    expose:
      - "4000"
    environment: *backend-env
    volumes:
      - media_data:/app/media
    depends_on:
      migrate:
        condition: service_completed_successfully
      qdrant:
        condition: service_healthy
      ml-service:
        condition: service_healthy
    healthcheck:
      # 127.0.0.1, not localhost: /etc/hosts maps localhost to both 127.0.0.1
      # and ::1, and BusyBox wget tries only the first address it gets. The
      # server binds IPv4 only, so the IPv6 attempt is refused and the service
      # never turns healthy.
      test:
        ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://127.0.0.1:4000/api/v1/health || exit 1"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5
      start_period: 15s

  # Same image as `backend`, runs the pg-boss job loop instead of the HTTP server.
  worker:
    <<: *backend-build
    restart: unless-stopped
    command: ["npm", "run", "start:worker"]
    environment: *backend-env
    volumes:
      - media_data:/app/media
    depends_on:
      migrate:
        condition: service_completed_successfully
      qdrant:
        condition: service_healthy
      ml-service:
        condition: service_healthy
    healthcheck:
      # The worker serves nothing but this probe (see worker.ts). start_period is
      # longer than the backend's because crash recovery runs before the health
      # server binds. See the backend healthcheck for why this is not localhost.
      test:
        ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://127.0.0.1:4001/api/v1/health || exit 1"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5
      start_period: 30s

  # Next.js dashboard. Build context is repo root (needs backend/workspaces/backend-api-types).
  # NEXT_PUBLIC_CORE_BACKEND_DOMAIN is baked into the client bundle at build time.
  dashboard:
    image: daz-pilot-dashboard:latest
    build:
      context: .
      dockerfile: dashboard/Dockerfile
      args:
        NEXT_PUBLIC_CORE_BACKEND_DOMAIN: ${NEXT_PUBLIC_CORE_BACKEND_DOMAIN:-http://localhost:4000}
    restart: unless-stopped
    expose:
      - "3000"
    # next.config.ts calls validateEnv() on `next start` too, so the same URLs
    # must be present at runtime — not only as build args.
    environment:
      NODE_ENV: production
      PORT: 3000
      CORE_BACKEND_DOMAIN: http://backend:4000
      NEXT_PUBLIC_CORE_BACKEND_DOMAIN: ${NEXT_PUBLIC_CORE_BACKEND_DOMAIN:-http://localhost:4000}
      SCHOOL_SLUG: ${SCHOOL_SLUG:-}
    depends_on:
      backend:
        condition: service_healthy
    healthcheck:
      test:
        [
          "CMD-SHELL",
          "wget -qO- http://127.0.0.1:3000/ >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 1",
        ]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5
      start_period: 20s

  # Online backups of postgres, qdrant and media_data. Starts with the stack and
  # runs on BACKUP_SCHEDULE; needs AGE_RECIPIENT in .env or it exits immediately.
  # Manual run:  docker compose run --rm backup backup.sh
  # See infra/backup/BACKUP.md. Excluded from the hot-reload dev override.
  backup:
    image: daz-pilot-backup:latest
    build:
      context: ./infra/backup
      dockerfile: Dockerfile
    restart: unless-stopped
    init: true
    environment:
      DB_HOST: postgres
      DB_PORT: 5432
      DB_USER: ${DB_USER}
      DB_PASS: ${DB_PASS}
      DB_NAME: ${DB_NAME}
      DB_SSL: ${DB_SSL:-false}
      QDRANT_HOST: qdrant
      QDRANT_PORT: 6333
      BACKUP_SCHEDULE: ${BACKUP_SCHEDULE:-0 3 * * *}
      BACKUP_RETENTION_DAYS: ${BACKUP_RETENTION_DAYS:-30}
      BACKUP_ALLOW_PLAINTEXT: ${BACKUP_ALLOW_PLAINTEXT:-false}
      BACKUP_QDRANT_TIMEOUT_SEC: ${BACKUP_QDRANT_TIMEOUT_SEC:-600}
      AGE_RECIPIENT: ${AGE_RECIPIENT:-}
      AGE_IDENTITY_FILE: ${AGE_IDENTITY_FILE:-}
      TZ: ${TZ:-UTC}
    volumes:
      - backup_data:/backups
      - media_data:/media
      - qdrant_snapshots:/qdrant-snapshots
    depends_on:
      postgres:
        condition: service_healthy
      qdrant:
        condition: service_healthy

volumes:
  postgres_data:
  qdrant_storage:
  qdrant_snapshots:
  ml_model_cache:
  media_data:
  backup_data:

# Local overlay: publishes the service ports on the host so the stack is usable
# from a browser, curl or a natively running backend.
#
#   docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.local.yml up --build
#   (npm run docker:local)
#
# Only for a personal machine. On a server the base file stays as it is and a
# reverse proxy joins the compose network instead — publishing Postgres or the
# ML service there would put them on a public interface.

services:
  # 5433 by default so a Postgres already running on the host's 5432 does not
  # collide. Native backend dev connects here (backend/.env: DB_PORT=5433).
  postgres:
    ports:
      - "${POSTGRES_PORT:-5433}:5432"

  ml-service:
    ports:
      - "${ML_SERVICE_PORT:-8000}:8000"

  backend:
    ports:
      - "${BACKEND_PORT:-4000}:4000"

  dashboard:
    ports:
      - "${DASHBOARD_PORT:-3000}:3000"
=== DEV ===
# Dev override: hot-reload for backend, worker and ml-service.
# Source is mounted live — no rebuild needed on code changes.
#
# Stacks on top of the local overlay, which publishes the host ports:
#   docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.local.yml \
#     -f docker-compose.dev.yml up --build
#   (npm run docker:dev)
#
# Start deps only with ml-service hot-reload (backend natively):
#   docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.local.yml \
#     -f docker-compose.dev.yml up postgres qdrant ml-service -d

services:
  # tsx watch: restarts the API server on any source change under backend/.
  backend:
    build:
      context: ./backend
      dockerfile: Dockerfile.dev
    image: daz-pilot-backend:dev
    command: ["npm", "run", "dev:core_backend"]
    volumes:
      - ./backend:/app
      # Keep the container's node_modules — don't let the host mount shadow them.
      - /app/node_modules
    environment:
      NODE_ENV: development

  # tsx watch: same image as `backend` dev build, watches worker.ts.
  worker:
    build:
      context: ./backend

## Projektbeschreibung

In Berufsschulklassen mit DaZ (Deutsch als Zweitsprache) oder DaF (Deutsch als Fremdsprache) erleben Lehrkräfte regelmäßig, wie fachsprachliche Barrieren den Unterrichtsfluss behindern. Auf den Niveaus A2–B1 fehlen niedrigschwellige, fachspezifische Lernangebote, die direkt in den Schulalltag integriert sind.

**DaZ-Pilot** ist ein digitaler Sprach-Copilot für inklusiven Berufsschulunterricht. Die App verbindet Bilderkennung, Fachwortschatz-Training, Audio-Aussprache und Gamification, um Sprachbarrieren abzubauen und den Ausbildungs­erfolg zu steigern. Lehrkräfte erhalten ein Dashboard zur Analyse von Lernständen und zur Erweiterung des Fachwortschatzes.

Die Lösung ist datenschutzfreundlich, vollständig auf Schulinfrastruktur (Moodle) abgestimmt und unter der EUPL-Lizenz quelloffen verfügbar.

## Zielgruppe

| Rolle                              | Nutzung                                                                              |
| ---------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **Schüler:innen** (DaZ/DaF, A2–B1) | App: Objekte erkennen, Vokabeltraining, Quiz                                         |
| **Lehrkräfte**                     | Dashboard: Arbeitsaufträge verwalten, Lernfortschritt einsehen, Fachbegriffe pflegen |
| **Schuladministration / IT**       | On-Premises Deployment oder SaaS-Variante                                            |

Die Lösung ist für alle 34 Regionalen Berufsbildungszentren (RBZ) und Berufsschulen in Schleswig-Holstein konzipiert und auf andere Bundesländer sowie Gemeinschaftsschulen übertragbar.

## Kernfunktionen

### Fachbegriffe visuell erkennen

Schüler:innen richten die Gerätekamera auf Werkzeuge oder Unterrichtsgegenstände. Ist der Begriff in der zentralen Datenbank hinterlegt, werden Bild, Begriff, Artikel sowie Singular- und Pluralform sofort angezeigt. Basis: **SigLIP** (Open-Source-Bilderkennung).

### Arbeitsaufträge mit integriertem Vokabeltraining

Dokumente in Moodle mit dem Dateinamen-Tag `[DAZP]` werden automatisch per **Tesseract OCR** nach Fachbegriffen durchsucht. Ein passender QR-Code wird in die PDF eingefügt und mit dem jeweiligen Vokabeltraining verknüpft – ohne Mehraufwand für Lehrkräfte.

### Audioausgabe für Fachbegriffe

Richtige Aussprache (inkl. Artikel, Singular, Plural) über **On-Device TTS** – offline, ohne externe Dienste, datenschutzkonform.

### Personalisierte Anmeldung

Login mit dem bestehenden Schul-Account via **OpenID Connect** (z. B. über Keycloak) – keine separate Registrierung, nutzbar auch auf Schulgeräten.

### Nachbereitungsmodus mit Gamification

Vokabeltraining und Quizfunktionen zur Festigung nach dem Unterricht. Fortschritte, Punkte und Abzeichen motivieren Lernende zur regelmäßigen Wiederholung.

### Lehrkräfte-Dashboard & Analyse

Klassenübersichten, Schwierigkeitsanalysen, Upload & Verwaltung von Arbeitsaufträgen und direkte Pflege der zentralen Fachbegriffs-Datenbank.

## Deployment

### Produktionsbetrieb (Docker)

```sh
# Repository klonen
git clone https://gitlab.opencode.de/sh/digitalhub-sh/landesprogramm-offene-innovationen/daz-pilot.git
cd daz-pilot

# Compose-Variablen setzen

```

Der Stack veröffentlicht keine Host-Ports. Erreichbar wird er über einen Reverse
Proxy, der dem Compose-Netz beitritt und auf `backend:4000` und `dashboard:3000`
routet — siehe [INSTALLATION.md](INSTALLATION.md).

> API, Worker und DB-Migrator teilen sich **ein** Image (`backend/Dockerfile`);
> die Migration läuft als einmaliger Job vor dem Backend-Start.

Vor dem ersten Start anzupassen:

| Variable                                    | Warum                                                                                                    |
| ------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `SUPER_ADMIN_API_KEY`, `SECRETS_ENCRYPTION_KEY` | Die Vorgabewerte stehen öffentlich im Repository.                                                      |
| `MEDIA_URL_SIGNING_KEY`                     | Dito. `openssl rand -base64 32`.                                                                          |
| `DB_PASS`                                   | Dito.                                                                                                      |
| `CORE_BACKEND_DOMAIN`, `FRONTEND_DOMAIN`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_CORE_BACKEND_DOMAIN` | Öffentliche URLs. Die letzte wird beim Build in das Dashboard-Bundle kompiliert. |
| `SMTP_*`                                    | Ohne erreichbaren Mailserver funktioniert der E-Mail-Login nicht.                                        |
| `TRUST_PROXY`                               | Anzahl der Reverse-Proxies vor der API.                                                                   |
| `AUTH_RATE_LIMIT_MAX`                       | Standard 60 pro IP und 15 Minuten. Eine Klasse hinter einer NAT-IP teilt sich dieses Kontingent.         |

### Compose-Dateien

| Datei                        | Zweck                                                                                                    |
| ---------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `docker-compose.yml`         | Der Stack, ohne veröffentlichte Host-Ports (`npm run docker:up`). Diese Datei geht unverändert auf den Server. |
| `docker-compose.local.yml`   | Legt die Host-Ports drauf, damit der Stack auf dem Arbeitsrechner per `localhost` erreichbar ist (`npm run docker:local`). Nie auf einem Server. |
| `docker-compose.dev.yml`     | Hot-Reload für Backend, Worker und ML-Service. Setzt auf dem Local-Overlay auf (`npm run docker:dev`).    |
| `docker-compose.test.yml`    | Wegwerf-Postgres für die Testsuite, Daten in tmpfs.                                                      |
| `docker-compose.override.yml`| Persönliche Ergänzungen, gitignored, wird ohne `-f` automatisch geladen.                                  |

Der `backup`-Service startet mit dem Stack und sichert PostgreSQL, Qdrant und
`media_data` im laufenden Betrieb (keine Downtime, Standard 03:00 UTC). Er
benötigt `AGE_RECIPIENT` in `.env` — ohne Schlüssel beendet er sich sofort mit
einer Meldung im Log. Coolify braucht keine Sonderintegration.

```sh
# Schlüssel erzeugen, öffentlichen Teil als AGE_RECIPIENT in .env eintragen
docker run --rm daz-pilot-backup:latest age-keygen > age-identity.txt
```

=== backend/Dockerfile ===
# Single image for all three Node processes in the stack: the HTTP API
# (start:core_backend), the pg-boss job worker (start:worker) and the one-shot
# DB migrator (start:migrate). The compose file runs the same image and only
# swaps the `command`, so build + cache are shared across backend/worker/migrate.
#
# Build context is `backend/` (see docker-compose.yml in the repo root). The image mirrors
# ml-service/Dockerfile's co-located convention.

# ---- Stage 1: Install all dependencies ----
FROM node:22-alpine AS deps

WORKDIR /app

COPY package.json package-lock.json ./
COPY workspaces/backend-api-types/package.json ./workspaces/backend-api-types/
COPY workspaces/backend-utils/package.json ./workspaces/backend-utils/
COPY workspaces/database/package.json ./workspaces/database/
COPY workspaces/core-backend/package.json ./workspaces/core-backend/
COPY workspaces/database-migrator/package.json ./workspaces/database-migrator/

RUN npm ci

# ---- Stage 2: Build TypeScript ----
FROM deps AS build

COPY tsconfig.base.json tsconfig.json ./
COPY workspaces/ ./workspaces/

RUN npm run build

# ---- Stage 3: Production image ----
FROM node:22-alpine AS production

WORKDIR /app

# ffmpeg is used by core-backend for video frame extraction (see videoFrames.ts).
# mupdf-tools (mutool) + tesseract-ocr are used by the assignment OCR pipeline
# (see utils/ocr/ocr.ts); the `deu` traineddata is required by its `-l deu` flag.
# wget is used by the compose healthcheck.
RUN apk add --no-cache ffmpeg mupdf-tools tesseract-ocr tesseract-ocr-data-deu wget

COPY --from=deps /app/package.json /app/package-lock.json ./
COPY --from=deps /app/workspaces/backend-api-types/package.json ./workspaces/backend-api-types/
COPY --from=deps /app/workspaces/backend-utils/package.json ./workspaces/backend-utils/
COPY --from=deps /app/workspaces/database/package.json ./workspaces/database/
COPY --from=deps /app/workspaces/core-backend/package.json ./workspaces/core-backend/
COPY --from=deps /app/workspaces/database-migrator/package.json ./workspaces/database-migrator/

RUN npm ci --omit=dev

COPY --from=build /app/workspaces/backend-api-types/dist/ ./workspaces/backend-api-types/dist/
COPY --from=build /app/workspaces/backend-utils/dist/ ./workspaces/backend-utils/dist/
COPY --from=build /app/workspaces/database/dist/ ./workspaces/database/dist/
COPY --from=build /app/workspaces/core-backend/dist/ ./workspaces/core-backend/dist/
COPY --from=build /app/workspaces/database-migrator/dist/ ./workspaces/database-migrator/dist/

# Media storage for locally-persisted technical term images & videos. The
# compose file mounts a named volume here; the directory matches the default
# MEDIA_STORAGE_DIR env var.
#
# Ownership must be set before the VOLUME line: Docker copies the image
# directory's ownership onto a named volume only when it first creates it, so
# volumes that already exist need a manual chown (see README).
RUN mkdir -p /app/media && chown node:node /app/media
VOLUME ["/app/media"]

ENV NODE_ENV=production
ENV MEDIA_STORAGE_DIR=/app/media
EXPOSE 4000

# `node` (uid 1000) ships with the base image. Runtime writes only ever target
# /app/media and os.tmpdir(), and 4000/4001 are unprivileged, so nothing here
# needs root — while ffmpeg/mutool/tesseract parse untrusted uploads, which is
# the surface this limits. Applies to the worker and migrate services too;
# they reuse this image and override only the command.
USER node

# Default process is the HTTP API. The `worker` and `migrate` compose services
# override this with `npm run start:worker` / `npm run start:migrate`.
CMD ["npm", "run", "start:core_backend"]

FROM python:3.11-slim

WORKDIR /app

RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends build-essential curl && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

COPY requirements.txt .
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir torch torchvision --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu && \
    pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt

COPY . .

# python:3.11-slim ships no unprivileged account, so create one. The only
# runtime write target is the HuggingFace cache (HF_HOME, a named volume in
# compose); code in /app and site-packages stay root-owned and read-only.
# Ownership must be set here so Docker copies it onto the volume when it first
# creates it — pre-existing ml_model_cache volumes need a manual chown (see README).
RUN useradd --create-home --uid 1000 --shell /usr/sbin/nologin app && \
    mkdir -p /cache/huggingface && \
    chown -R app:app /cache/huggingface

USER app

EXPOSE 8000

HEALTHCHECK --interval=30s --timeout=5s --start-period=180s --retries=3 \
  CMD curl -fsS http://localhost:8000/health || exit 1

CMD ["uvicorn", "main:app", "--host", "0.0.0.0", "--port", "8000"]

=== BACKUP.md head ===
# Online backups (Postgres, Qdrant, media)

DaZ-Pilot writes three persistent stores. This sidecar backs them up **without stopping** the API, worker, dashboard, or ML service.

| Store            | How                                                      | Runtime impact                                               |
| ---------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| PostgreSQL       | `pg_dump -Fc` (transaction snapshot)                     | None. Writers continue.                                      |
| Qdrant           | One snapshot per collection via HTTP, plus the alias map | None (hot snapshots).                                        |
| `media_data`     | `tar` of the live volume                                 | Files written _during_ the tar may be missing or incomplete. |
| `ml_model_cache` | Not backed up                                            | Re-downloaded from Hugging Face.                             |

**Why per-collection and not a full storage snapshot:** Qdrant can _create_ a full storage snapshot over HTTP, but it can only _restore_ one through the CLI at startup (`qdrant --storage-snapshot ...`). Only collection snapshots have a recover endpoint. Per-collection snapshots therefore keep restore possible against the running Qdrant of this stack. The alias map (`school_<uuid>` → `school_<uuid>__v<timestamp>`) is captured separately from `GET /aliases`, since collection snapshots do not carry aliases.

There is **no distributed freeze** across the three stores. Dump, Qdrant snapshot, and tar run one after another, so a few seconds to minutes of cross-store drift is possible (e.g. ingest finished in Qdrant before Postgres recorded the job). Account and learning data live in Postgres; ML drift is repairable by re-ingest/training. **Do not mix artifacts from different sets** on restore.

Restore **does** require a maintenance window. See [RESTORE.md](RESTORE.md).

The only interface is **Docker Compose**. Coolify (or any other wrapper) just runs this file; there are no Coolify-specific scripts.

## Starting it

The `backup` service is part of the stack, so it starts with everything else:

```sh
docker compose up -d --build
```

It then runs on `BACKUP_SCHEDULE` (default 03:00 UTC) inside the container. Coolify needs no special handling — it deploys this same file.

**It refuses to start without `AGE_RECIPIENT`** (see below). That is deliberate: a misconfigured key should surface at deploy time, not at 03:00. Check with `docker compose logs backup`.

Manual run, any time, alongside the scheduler:

```sh
docker compose run --rm backup backup.sh
```

The hot-reload dev stack (`-f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.dev.yml`) excludes the service via profile `ops`; add `--profile ops` there if you want to exercise it locally.

## Encryption

Backups are encrypted with [age](https://github.com/FiloSottile/age). Generate a key pair on a trusted machine (not necessarily the app host):

```sh
age-keygen -o age-identity.txt
# public key is printed and stored in the file as `# public key: age1...`
```

Put the **public** key in `.env` as `AGE_RECIPIENT`. Keep `age-identity.txt` **off the app server** if you can; you only need it for restore. Never commit the identity.

Several recipients: comma-separated `AGE_RECIPIENT`.

Local drills without keys (plaintext, throwaway data only):

```env
BACKUP_ALLOW_PLAINTEXT=true
```

Without `AGE_RECIPIENT` and without that flag, the container exits on start and `backup.sh` refuses to run.

# because the dashboard depends on the backend workspace package
# `@daz-pilot/daz-pilot-backend-api-types` via a `file:` path. That package must
# be built first so the `file:` install resolves to compiled output.

# ---- Stage 1: Build the shared api-types package ----
FROM node:22-alpine AS apitypes

WORKDIR /repo/backend

COPY backend/package.json backend/package-lock.json ./
COPY backend/workspaces/backend-api-types/package.json ./workspaces/backend-api-types/
COPY backend/workspaces/backend-utils/package.json ./workspaces/backend-utils/
COPY backend/workspaces/database/package.json ./workspaces/database/
COPY backend/workspaces/core-backend/package.json ./workspaces/core-backend/
COPY backend/workspaces/database-migrator/package.json ./workspaces/database-migrator/

RUN npm ci

COPY backend/tsconfig.base.json backend/tsconfig.json ./
COPY backend/workspaces/backend-api-types/ ./workspaces/backend-api-types/

RUN npm run build --workspace=@daz-pilot/daz-pilot-backend-api-types

# ---- Stage 2: Install dashboard deps & build ----
FROM node:22-alpine AS build

WORKDIR /repo/dashboard

# The `file:` dependency resolves to ../backend/workspaces/backend-api-types, so
# the built package must sit at that path before `npm ci`.
COPY --from=apitypes /repo/backend/workspaces/backend-api-types /repo/backend/workspaces/backend-api-types

# .npmrc sets `install-links=true`, which makes npm copy the `file:` dependency
# into node_modules (instead of symlinking). The lockfile was generated with this
# setting, so npm ci needs it to stay in sync — and it makes the build/runtime
# self-contained (no symlink to the backend workspace at runtime).
COPY dashboard/package.json dashboard/package-lock.json dashboard/.npmrc ./
RUN npm ci

COPY dashboard/ ./

# next.config.ts runs validateEnv() at build time, so every URL in envSchema must
# be present. NEXT_PUBLIC_* is inlined into the client bundle, so these must point
# at the host-facing URLs. Override via build args if needed.
ARG NEXT_PUBLIC_CORE_BACKEND_DOMAIN=http://localhost:4000
ENV NEXT_PUBLIC_CORE_BACKEND_DOMAIN=$NEXT_PUBLIC_CORE_BACKEND_DOMAIN
ENV CORE_BACKEND_DOMAIN=$NEXT_PUBLIC_CORE_BACKEND_DOMAIN

RUN npm run build

# ---- Stage 3: Production runtime (next start) ----
FROM node:22-alpine AS production

WORKDIR /repo/dashboard

ENV NODE_ENV=production
ENV PORT=3000

# install-links=true copied api-types into node_modules, so the built app is
# self-contained — no backend workspace needed at runtime.
COPY --from=build /repo/dashboard /repo/dashboard

# `next start` writes only under .next/cache at runtime (the <Image> optimizer
# caches fetched /media/** responses there, see images.remotePatterns). Only that
# subtree is handed to `node`; app code and node_modules stay root-owned and
# therefore read-only to the runtime user.
RUN mkdir -p .next/cache && chown -R node:node .next/cache

EXPOSE 3000

# `node` (uid 1000) ships with the base image. Port 3000 is unprivileged and no
# runtime write lands outside .next/cache, so the server needs no root.
USER node

CMD ["npm", "run", "start"]

# Only for a personal machine. On a server the base file stays as it is and a
# reverse proxy joins the compose network instead — publishing Postgres or the
# ML service there would put them on a public interface.

services:
  # 5433 by default so a Postgres already running on the host's 5432 does not
  # collide. Native backend dev connects here (backend/.env: DB_PORT=5433).
  postgres:
    ports:
      - "${POSTGRES_PORT:-5433}:5432"

  ml-service:
    ports:
      - "${ML_SERVICE_PORT:-8000}:8000"

  backend:
    ports:
      - "${BACKEND_PORT:-4000}:4000"

  dashboard:
    ports:
      - "${DASHBOARD_PORT:-3000}:3000"
